title: Brighten a photo with an adjustment
summary: Add a Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer and compare before and after.

steps.say: Make sure a photo is open and its layer is highlighted in the Layers panel.

check.prompt: Is a photo open with its layer highlighted in the Layers panel?

hints: Click the photo's row in the Layers panel to highlight it.
Open a photo with Control O if none is showing.
steps.why: The new adjustment goes right above the highlighted layer.

steps.say: Open the Layer menu, choose New Adjustment Layer, then Brightness/Contrast.

checks.prompt: Is a New Layer dialog open, or a Brightness/Contrast layer listed in the Layers panel?

hints: The half black, half white circle at the bottom of the Layers panel opens the same list.
The Adjustments panel on the right has a Brightness/Contrast button too.
steps.why: An adjustment layer changes the look without altering the photo itself.

steps.say: If a New Layer dialog appears, click OK.

check.prompt: Is a Brightness/Contrast adjustment layer listed in the Layers panel?

hints: The dialog only appears when you use the menu; the panel button skips it.
Press Enter to click OK from the keyboard.
steps.why: The dialog only names the new layer.

steps.say: In the Properties panel, drag the Brightness slider to the right until the photo looks lighter.

check.prompt: Does the photo look brighter than it did at the start of this step?

hints: You can type a number such as 30 in the box next to Brightness.
If the Properties panel is hidden, double-click the adjustment layer's icon.
steps.why: Brightness lifts the middle tones of the whole photo.

steps.say: Now drag the Contrast slider a little to the right for punchier colors.

check.prompt: Does the photo show stronger contrast than it did at the start of this step?

hints: Small changes, around 10 to 20, usually look best.
Typing a value in the Contrast box works too.
steps.why: Contrast spreads lights and darks further apart.

steps.say: Click the eye icon next to the adjustment layer to compare before and after.

checks.prompt: Has the adjustment been switched off so the photo looks like the original again?

hints: Click the eye again to turn the adjustment back on.
Say done when you have compared both versions.
steps.why: Adjustment layers can be switched off or changed later, which keeps the original safe.
